indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.1.1.2: Understand the differences between living things, non-living things, and things which have never been alive
indicator.objective: Know the basic needs of living things (food, water and air)

skills.description: Identify food, water and air as basic needs
Give examples of living things and say what they need
Explain simply why living things need food, water and air

misconceptions: Only people need food, water and air.
Shelter and toys are basic needs.
Plants get all their food from the soil only.
Air is not needed because we cannot see it.

questions.stem: What do all living things need to stay alive?
questions.explanation: Food is a basic need for all living things. Toys, cars, and shoes are not needed for survival.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose toys because they like them, but toys are not a basic need.

questions.stem: Which of these is a basic need of a plant?
questions.explanation: Plants need water to grow. They do not need meat, books, or milk.
questions.misconception: Pupils might choose meat because animals eat meat.

questions.stem: To stay alive, people need to breathe...
hints: You do this all the time without thinking.
questions.explanation: People need air to breathe. We cannot see air, but we need it to live.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose water because they know it is a basic need, but the question asks what we breathe.

questions.stem: Which of these living things needs food?
questions.explanation: A dog is a living thing and needs food to survive. Stones, cups, and chairs are non-living.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think non-living things like cars need food because they need fuel.

questions.stem: Why do we drink water?
hints: You feel thirsty when you need it.
questions.explanation: We drink water because it is a basic need that keeps us alive and healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think we only drink water for fun or because we are thirsty, missing the survival aspect.

questions.stem: A potted plant is not watered for many days. What is it missing?
hints: What do you give a plant to help it grow?
questions.explanation: The plant is missing water. Without water, plants will wilt and die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants only need soil and forget that they need water.

questions.stem: Which of these living things needs water to survive?
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water and needs water to survive. Stones, pencils, and books are non-living.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all animals only need food and forget about water.

questions.stem: Why do we need air?
hints: You do this with your nose and mouth.
questions.explanation: We need air to breathe. Breathing keeps us alive.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the need for air with the need for food or water.

questions.stem: Name two things a baby needs to stay alive.
questions.explanation: A baby needs food (milk), water, and air to stay alive and grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may list toys or clothes instead of basic needs.

questions.stem: Give one example of a living thing and say what it eats.
questions.explanation: A goat is a living thing that eats grass.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name a non-living thing like a car.

questions.stem: Kofi has a plant, a dog, and a fish. What do all three need?
questions.explanation: Plants, dogs, and fish are all living things, so they all need water. Meat, bones, and grass are specific to certain animals.
questions.misconception: Pupils may focus on the dog or fish and choose meat or bones.

questions.stem: Ama has a cat, a bird, and a fish. Which one needs air but does NOT live on land?
questions.explanation: A fish lives in water but still needs air (from the water) to breathe. It does not live on land.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish do not need air because they live in water.

questions.stem: Explain why a person cannot live without water.

criteria.description: States that we need water to drink
States that water keeps us alive or healthy

hints: Think about what happens when you are very thirsty.
questions.explanation: This tests the understanding of water as a basic need.

questions.stem: What happens to a plant if it does not get air?
hints: Without it, living things cannot survive.
questions.explanation: Plants need air to survive. Without air, a plant will die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think plants do not need air because they are not animals.

questions.stem: Which of these things needs food?
hints: It cries when it is hungry.
questions.explanation: A baby is a living thing and needs food to grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think objects that 'use up' things (like a car using fuel) need food.

questions.stem: A farmer gives his goats food, water, and a place to sleep. But the goats are still dying. What basic need is missing?
questions.explanation: All living things need air. If the goats are in a place without fresh air, they will die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think shelter or water is missing because those are visible, but air is invisible yet essential.

questions.stem: Why is food important for living things?
options: It gives them energy to grow and work
hints: What happens when you don't eat?
questions.explanation: Food gives living things the energy they need to grow, move, and stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think food is just for satisfying hunger without understanding its role in energy.

questions.stem: Draw a living thing and write two things it needs to survive.

criteria.description: Writes one correct need (e.g., food, water, air)

hints: Draw a plant or an animal.
What does it need to live?
questions.explanation: This tests drawing and recall of basic needs.

questions.stem: Tell me three things that all living things need to survive.
questions.explanation: This tests verbal recall of the three basic needs.

questions.stem: A fish is taken out of water and placed on a table. What will happen to the fish and why?
options: It will die because it cannot breathe
It will turn into a stone
questions.explanation: A fish needs water to breathe. On a table, it cannot get the water it needs and will die.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fish can breathe air on land like humans.
